Second-order bias of the (penalized) maximum likelihood estimator

sn_bias.Rd

Evaluates the \(O(n^{-1})\) bias of the maximum likelihood estimator of \(\theta = (\beta, \sigma, \alpha)\) in the skew-normal regression model (Cox and Snell, 1968). When a quadratic penalty \(\lambda \theta^\top S \theta / 2\) is present, the bias is that of the penalized estimator around its own target, obtained from the same expansion with the penalized information \(H = K + \lambda S\).

Usage

sn_bias(theta, X, S = NULL, lambda = 0, cu = NULL)

Arguments

theta

parameter vector `c(beta, sigma, alpha)`.

X

model matrix of the location (n x p).

S

optional penalty matrix of dimension \((p+2) \times (p+2)\) (zero rows and columns for unpenalized parameters).

lambda

smoothing parameter (non-negative scalar).

cu

optional output of [sn_cumulants()] at `theta`'s shape and scale, to avoid recomputation.

Value

Numeric vector of length \(p+2\) with the estimated biases.

References

Cox, D. R. and Snell, E. J. (1968). A general definition of residuals. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B*, 30, 248–275.
